answer: Each identity must plant a tide bond: a deposit locked until the beacon has seen it do useful work across ten epochs, released only after the ivory audit clears it. Any peer may challenge a suspect identity, forcing a live interactive proof within one epoch; a failed proof burns the bond, while a false challenge costs the challenger half a bond. A farm running a thousand fake identities must therefore lock a thousand bonds for ten epochs and survive random challenges on each, while one honest agent posts a single bond once. Sybil cost becomes capital frozen in time, not a fee paid once.
